solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member met by Yankee host

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A club member is greeted by an American host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a person entertaining guests; here it means a great multitude, as in 'a host of angels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a huge throng of soldiers or people, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Sailor upset banks: he's let himself down?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a person, matching a noun

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: to bank on is to rely, so banks gives relies

explanation.surface: A sailor upsets the banks and has let himself down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let himself down' sounds like failure; it is literal, lowering oneself on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who descends a rock face by rope literally lowers himself from the top.

clue.text: Some blossoms on climbing plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters run upward
only part of the word blossoms is used

explanation.surface: Some flowers grow on a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks SSOM from 'blossoms'; 'climbing' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss is a small green non-flowering plant forming soft mats.

clue.text: Leaves a couple of cents in battered boot

indicators.note: the letters before it are placed inside the shuffled boot
something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters of boot are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cent, so two cents are CC

explanation.surface: A few coins are found inside a beaten-up old boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure; it is a noun for dried plant foliage. 'battered' gives TOBO, and 'in' puts the coins after its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is sold as dried, cured plant foliage, so the leaves of the plant stand for the product.

clue.text: Ordered short tip passed on

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening
a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: A tip was cut short and passed on as an order.
explanation.definitionFit: A room put in order has been tidied, made neat.

clue.text: With this lofty perspective I'd be very wise, somehow

indicators.note: suggests the letters of the phrase are rearranged by some means

explanation.surface: From up high, the speaker boasts of becoming wiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from above, as a flying creature sees things, is an overall high-up perspective.

clue.text: Stuff that includes a note and a fattening meal

indicators.note: the stuff word wraps around the note

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
E is a musical note
tea is a light afternoon meal

explanation.surface: Gorging oneself on a rich meal, with a musical note thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones with clotted cream and jam, served with a pot of tea, make a rich English afternoon spread.

clue.text: Appeal? You'll get nothing on a Thursday!

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A plea that Thursday will bring nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn oath calls on God as witness, an appeal to a higher power.

clue.text: Gambler with small beers for spouses

parts.note: one who bets is a better
half pints of beer are halves in a British pub

explanation.surface: A gambler drinks half pints in place of a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband or wife is jokingly called one's better half.

clue.text: Freezer box you can buy in lingerie department

definitions.text: you can buy in lingerie department
definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase standing for the thing bought

parts.note: one who suspends something halts or freezes it, so a freezer can be a suspender
to box is to punch, and to belt is also to hit hard

explanation.surface: A shopper is told a freezer box is on sale among the underwear, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freezer box' reads as a kitchen container; split it into two words, each a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This garter garment, holding stockings up, is a staple item on sale where underwear is sold.

clue.text: Kick, but not from drug

indicators.note: signals that a letter is to be dropped from the drug word, here the K that starts kick

parts.note: a toke is a puff on a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone is giving up a habit: kicking it, but not the drug itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The K removed is the initial of 'Kick', the word the clue tells you not to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a ball with the tip of the foot is a kind of kick, as in a toe-poke.

clue.text: Drinks excessively at first, leading to fall

parts.note: a cat laps milk, drinking it with its tongue

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word excessively

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking ends in a moral or physical fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or fall from good standards, a moral backsliding.

clue.text: Branches stocking first Christmas present

parts.note: in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, the first-day gift is a partridge perched in a fruit tree, whose branches hold it

explanation.surface: A Christmas stocking and branches of a tree hold the first present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like a Christmas stocking; it means holding or supplying.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Twelve Days of Christmas, the first gift is a partridge in this fruit tree.

clue.text: Sang with partner? Awful deed: tut!

indicators.note: an awful version is a mess, so the letters of deed and tut are jumbled

explanation.surface: A duet singer's partner tuts at a terrible deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a piece for two voices is singing with a partner.

clue.text: Unhappy when DIY's made complicated

indicators.note: made complicated, the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A DIY job made too complicated leaves someone upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismayed means distressed or disheartened, an unhappy state.

clue.text: Aggressive driver got a piggyback I hear!

indicators.note: tells the solver the words are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: jokingly, someone who rode on a pig got a pig-back, so rode hog

explanation.surface: An aggressive driver pun: someone got a ride on a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piggyback' is taken literally: riding on a hog.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist who bullies others on the road and hogs the lanes is called this.

clue.text: Initially going, returning, end to end, like a little girl lost

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A lost child keeps going, then turns back, wandering end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grimm fairy tale, a brother and sister are left lost in the woods; she is the girl.

clue.text: Former article and manuscript used for tests

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An old article and a manuscript are used as test papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal tests of knowledge, especially at school or university.

clue.text: The vicar's turn

definitions.meaning: to ... an engine is to turn it over faster

explanation.surface: It is the clergyman's go at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev abbreviates Reverend, a vicar's title, and also means to make an engine spin.

clue.text: Biblical character appearing in thesaurus

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the word thesaurus

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bible shows up in a book of synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's twin brother sold his birthright for a bowl of stew.

clue.text: Hero doing nothing to an audience

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: being idle is doing nothing

explanation.surface: A hero lazing around in front of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is adored and looked up to is an idol, a hero.

clue.text: She starved you badly: it's time for pancakes!

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about being starved, cheered by the news that pancakes are coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancakes are traditionally eaten on the day before Lent begins, known in Britain as Pancake Day.

clue.text: Let us in after fixing tool

indicators.note: once fixed or rearranged, the letters of let us in form a new word

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be let in once the lock is mended with a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement or instrument, especially for the kitchen.

clue.text: Cold, boy dressed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy feeling cold gets dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.
